title: DNS & DHCP Troubleshooting
subject: Networking Services
description: Practice enterprise incident tickets using the 4-step workflow: Triage, Diagnosis, Fix (GUI), and Change Note.

tickets.title: Domain join fails for DEPOT-LT17 (SRV records not found)
tickets.summary: A new laptop at DEPOT-03 can resolve the domain name but fails domain join with 'cannot locate a domain controller'.

workflow.triage: Domain join wizard fails; ping to DC IP works; nslookup of the domain returns an IP.
workflow.diagnosis: Client cannot resolve required AD SRV records (e.g., _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs). Often caused by clients using non-AD DNS or missing SRV data in the zone.
workflow.fix: DNS Manager: verify SRV records in _msdcs.<domain>. Ensure clients receive only AD DNS servers (DHCP option 006). If SRV records are missing, remediate DC registration/zone replication.

tickets.title: Secure dynamic updates failing for roaming laptops
tickets.summary: Some domain-joined laptops do not register A/PTR records after moving between sites.

workflow.triage: Leases are normal but hostnames are missing/stale in DNS for a subset of clients.
workflow.diagnosis: With secure updates, the updating principal matters. DHCP update credentials are missing/incorrect, or stale record ownership blocks updates.
workflow.fix: DHCP MMC → Server Properties → DNS: configure credentials for DNS updates and enable dynamic update settings. In DNS, remove conflicting stale records or correct record security so updates can succeed.

validations: Review DHCP/DNS event logs for update failures
Verify record ownership/security for the hostname

tickets.title: CNAME alias resolves but app fails due to certificate mismatch
tickets.summary: Users access https://payroll.global-logistics.local (CNAME) and receive certificate name mismatch warnings.

workflow.triage: DNS resolves the alias to the correct server, but browsers warn about certificate mismatch.
workflow.diagnosis: DNS is correct; TLS certificate SAN does not include the alias name, causing validation failure.
workflow.fix: DNS MMC: confirm CNAME target. On the web server, install/bind a certificate that includes the alias in SAN (IIS Manager → Site Bindings → https).

validations: Browser test shows no warnings after binding update

tickets.title: Scavenging removed critical host record unexpectedly
tickets.summary: After enabling scavenging, SRV-PROD-SQL01 stopped resolving. Service owners report outage until record recreated.

workflow.triage: Name returns NXDOMAIN; record is missing in the zone.
workflow.diagnosis: Aging/scavenging settings are too aggressive, or the critical record had a timestamp and became eligible for scavenging.
workflow.fix: DNS MMC → Zone Properties → Aging/Scavenging: review intervals and eligibility. Recreate critical records as true static (no timestamp) where appropriate and align policy with lifecycle needs.

validations: Enable Advanced View and inspect record timestamps
Check DNS server event logs for scavenging events
Verify critical records persist after eligibility window

tickets.title: Scavenging not cleaning stale records (zone aging disabled)
tickets.summary: Thousands of stale workstation A records remain from previous imaging cycles; scavenging is enabled but nothing is removed.

workflow.triage: Old hostnames still resolve; collisions occur during re-imaging.
workflow.diagnosis: Server scavenging is enabled, but zone aging is not enabled, so records never become eligible for scavenging.
workflow.fix: DNS MMC → Zone Properties → Aging: enable aging and set no-refresh/refresh intervals. Confirm server scavenging schedule is enabled.

validations: Confirm scavenging events occur on schedule
Re-check stale records after interval passes

tickets.title: PTR records missing for DHCP clients; monitoring shows 'unknown host'
tickets.summary: Monitoring relies on reverse lookups to tag assets, but many addresses return NXDOMAIN for PTR.

workflow.triage: Reverse queries fail; some forward A records exist but PTR records do not.
workflow.diagnosis: Reverse zone missing or DHCP is not configured to create PTRs (and/or secure update credentials are missing).
workflow.fix: DNS MMC: create reverse lookup zone(s). DHCP MMC → Server Properties → DNS: enable A and PTR updates and configure secure update credentials if needed.

validations: Confirm DHCP creates both A and PTR for new leases
Review DHCP audit logs for DNS update results

tickets.title: Conditional forwarder points to retired resolver (partner domain fails)
tickets.summary: Integration jobs fail because vendor.partner.local stopped resolving after vendor DNS migration.

workflow.triage: Queries to vendor.partner.local time out; all other DNS works normally.
workflow.diagnosis: Conditional forwarder points to an unreachable/retired vendor resolver IP.
workflow.fix: DNS MMC → Conditional Forwarders: update IPs to current partner DNS servers and verify connectivity (UDP/TCP 53).

validations: Event logs show no forwarder timeout warnings

tickets.title: Clients get inconsistent answers due to duplicate authoritative zones
tickets.summary: api.prod.global-logistics.local resolves to different IPs depending on client subnet.

workflow.triage: Different clients get different IPs for the same name.
workflow.diagnosis: Multiple DNS servers host authoritative zones with the same name but different data/replication scope.
workflow.fix: Remove/disable conflicting zone or correct replication so only intended authoritative zone is used. Ensure DHCP option 006 points to correct DNS servers.

validations: nslookup from multiple subnets returns consistent IP
Confirm authoritative zone data matches expected records

tickets.title: Forwarder outage causes slow external lookups
tickets.summary: External domain lookups are slow or time out; internal name resolution remains normal.

workflow.triage: External lookups take several seconds; intermittent failures occur.
workflow.diagnosis: Forwarders are unreachable, causing repeated timeouts before fallback (or fallback is disabled).
workflow.fix: DNS MMC → Server Properties → Forwarders: replace/remove unreachable forwarders; verify fallback behavior (root hints) and upstream reachability.

validations: DNS event logs show reduced forwarder timeout warnings

tickets.title: CNAME chain still points users to old server after migration
tickets.summary: Users access erp.global-logistics.local but are routed to the retired server after an app migration.

workflow.triage: ERP name resolves, but users hit the old host.
workflow.diagnosis: CNAME points to another alias that still targets the old server (CNAME chain not updated).
workflow.fix: DNS MMC: update the CNAME to point directly to the new host FQDN or correct the intermediate alias. Remove unused legacy aliases.

validations: Application logs show traffic hitting new server

tickets.title: Secure updates blocked by stale record ownership after device replacement
tickets.summary: PRN-FLOOR3 was replaced, but the hostname still resolves to the old IP and the new device cannot register.

workflow.triage: Clients resolve PRN-FLOOR3 to old IP; new device fails to update the record.
workflow.diagnosis: Existing record ownership/ACL prevents overwrite under secure dynamic updates.
workflow.fix: DNS MMC: delete stale A/PTR record (or adjust record security). Allow DHCP/client to re-register using correct credentials.

tickets.title: Domain join fails because DHCP hands out public DNS
tickets.summary: New laptops can browse the internet but fail first-boot domain join until DNS is manually changed.

workflow.triage: Join fails; internet works; ipconfig shows public DNS servers.
workflow.diagnosis: DHCP scope option 006 is set to public DNS, which does not host AD SRV records.
workflow.fix: DHCP MMC → Scope Options: set option 006 to internal AD DNS servers. Renew lease and retry join.

tickets.title: Secure DNS updates failing after DHCP server rebuild
tickets.summary: After rebuilding SRV-DHCP1, leases work but DNS A/PTR registration fails across the org.

workflow.triage: Clients have IP connectivity but cannot be resolved by hostname; few new dynamic records appear.
workflow.diagnosis: DHCP DNS update credentials were not restored/configured after rebuild.
workflow.fix: DHCP MMC → Server Properties → DNS: configure dedicated credentials for secure DNS updates and verify permissions.

validations: New leases create A and PTR records
DHCP/DNS event logs show successful secure updates

tickets.title: SRV record lookup returns retired domain controller
tickets.summary: Clients intermittently try to contact SRV-DC04 during logon/GP processing and time out.

workflow.triage: Group Policy processing/logon slow; occasional timeouts contacting a DC name that should be decommissioned.
workflow.diagnosis: AD/DNS cleanup wasn’t completed; stale SRV records still advertise the retired DC.
workflow.fix: DNS MMC → _msdcs zone: remove SRV records referencing retired DC. Complete metadata cleanup and validate replication.

validations: SRV queries return only active DCs

tickets.title: Split-brain internal zone breaks public subdomain resolution
tickets.summary: Internal zone for global-logistics.com exists for internal apps, but careers.global-logistics.com fails for internal users.

workflow.triage: Internal clients get NXDOMAIN for public subdomains not defined internally.
workflow.diagnosis: Internal DNS is authoritative for global-logistics.com but lacks public subdomain records, so it answers negatively instead of forwarding.
workflow.fix: DNS MMC: revise split-brain approach (populate required records, use delegation/stub/conditional forwarders, or adjust naming).

validations: nslookup careers.global-logistics.com works from internal clients
Authoritative responses occur only for intended internal names

tickets.title: Scope exhaustion causes intermittent IP assignment failures
tickets.summary: In the warehouse VLAN, some devices fail to obtain IPs during peak shifts; others eventually get addresses.

workflow.triage: Clients show APIPA or repeated 'Identifying…'; scope utilization is near 100%.
workflow.diagnosis: Scope is exhausted due to insufficient pool, long lease duration for transient devices, or excessive reservations.
workflow.fix: DHCP MMC → Scope: review Scope Statistics, Address Pool, Exclusions, Reservations. Expand scope (or redesign subnet) and adjust lease duration as appropriate.

validations: DHCP audit log shows successful ACKs

tickets.title: MAC Allow filter blocks new printers from leasing
tickets.summary: A secure print VLAN uses an allow list. After deploying new printers, none obtain DHCP leases.

workflow.triage: New printers show no IP address; existing printers still work.
workflow.diagnosis: MAC allow filtering is enabled, but new printer MACs are not in the allow list.
workflow.fix: DHCP MMC → IPv4 → Filters → Allow: add the new printer MAC addresses and confirm allow filtering is intended.

validations: DHCP logs show leases issued to approved MACs

tickets.title: MAC Deny filter blocks an executive laptop unexpectedly
tickets.summary: An executive laptop cannot obtain an IP on HQ Wi-Fi while other users are fine.

workflow.triage: Laptop associates to Wi-Fi but gets APIPA.
workflow.diagnosis: Device MAC address is mistakenly on the deny list (or matches a blocked entry).
workflow.fix: DHCP MMC → IPv4 → Filters → Deny: remove incorrect MAC entry and document why.

validations: Deny list still blocks intended devices

tickets.title: Failover relationship unhealthy after patching (shared secret mismatch)
tickets.summary: After maintenance, renewals start failing intermittently and failover relationship shows warnings.

workflow.triage: Some clients fail to renew; failover shows communication retries.
workflow.diagnosis: Failover relationship configuration is inconsistent (shared secret mismatch) or partner settings drifted.
workflow.fix: DHCP MMC → Failover: validate partner settings/shared secret. Correct or recreate relationship. Verify both servers are authorized and reachable.

tickets.title: Hot standby failover does not serve leases during primary outage
tickets.summary: During planned outage of SRV-DHCP1, SRV-DHCP2 does not start serving leases quickly.

workflow.triage: Clients cannot renew or obtain new leases longer than expected.
workflow.diagnosis: Standby is not properly configured/authorized for the scope or relationship settings are incorrect.
workflow.fix: DHCP MMC → Failover settings: verify hot standby configuration and role assignment; confirm SRV-DHCP2 is authorized and relationship applies to the scope.

validations: Standby issues leases during simulated outage

tickets.title: New VLAN clients cannot get DHCP (relay agent missing)
tickets.summary: A new VLAN for IoT devices was created. Clients cannot obtain IPs from centralized DHCP.

workflow.triage: IoT clients show APIPA; DHCP server never sees DISCOVER packets from that subnet.
workflow.diagnosis: DHCP broadcasts do not cross subnets; gateway lacks DHCP relay/IP helper to forward requests.
workflow.fix: Configure DHCP relay (IP helper) on the VLAN gateway to forward to SRV-DHCP1. Ensure the scope exists and is active.

tickets.title: Scope options misconfigured: clients get wrong DNS servers
tickets.summary: Clients get IPs but cannot resolve internal names; external browsing works.

workflow.triage: Clients have IP/gateway but internal hostnames fail; ipconfig shows public DNS.
workflow.diagnosis: Scope option 006 (DNS Servers) is configured incorrectly.
workflow.fix: DHCP MMC → Scope Options: set option 006 to internal DNS servers, then renew leases.

tickets.title: Reservation not taking effect; device keeps getting random IP
tickets.summary: A lobby camera must have a fixed IP via reservation but keeps getting different addresses after reboot.

workflow.triage: Reservation exists, but device receives non-reserved address.
workflow.diagnosis: Reservation was created using the wrong identifier (wrong MAC/interface) or device uses a DHCP Client Identifier.
workflow.fix: DHCP MMC → Address Leases: locate the device identifier then recreate reservation using the correct identifier.

validations: Device receives reserved IP after renew

tickets.title: Rogue DHCP server causing conflicting leases
tickets.summary: Some clients get the wrong gateway/DNS and lose connectivity intermittently on OFFICE-20.

workflow.triage: Leases differ between clients; some show unexpected gateway/DNS values.
workflow.diagnosis: A rogue DHCP server is responding on the VLAN.
workflow.fix: Identify/remove the rogue DHCP source; enforce DHCP snooping/port security on switching. Confirm only SRV-DHCP1 serves the VLAN.

validations: Clients consistently receive leases from authorized DHCP
Packet capture shows only one DHCPOFFER source

tickets.title: Failover load balance split misconfigured; one server issues most leases
tickets.summary: After enabling DHCP failover, SRV-DHCP1 issues nearly all leases while SRV-DHCP2 issues very few.

workflow.triage: Lease distribution is skewed; partner sometimes shows warnings.
workflow.diagnosis: Load balance percentage is misconfigured or partner health/connectivity is inconsistent.
workflow.fix: DHCP MMC → Failover relationship: verify load balance percentage and partner health. Correct split and resolve connectivity issues.

validations: Lease distribution begins to match the split

tickets.title: Relay forwards requests but no offers (scope missing/inactive)
tickets.summary: Relay is configured. DHCP server sees requests from 10.80.0.0/24, but clients still cannot obtain an IP.

workflow.triage: DISCOVERs appear in logs, but no OFFERs are sent.
workflow.diagnosis: No matching scope exists for the subnet, or the scope is inactive.
workflow.fix: DHCP MMC: create/activate a scope for 10.80.0.0/24 and configure address pool/options.

tickets.title: Global allow filtering enabled; entire branch cannot lease
tickets.summary: All devices at BRANCH-03 fail DHCP after a MAC filtering pilot was enabled on the server.

workflow.triage: Branch devices show APIPA; relay and scopes exist.
workflow.diagnosis: Allow list enabled globally without onboarding branch MACs causes blanket denial.
workflow.fix: Adjust filtering strategy (scope/policy-based) or add required MACs to allow list. Document change and approvals as required.

tickets.title: DHCP server unauthorized after directory maintenance
tickets.summary: DHCP service is running but no new leases are issued after AD maintenance.

workflow.triage: Clients get APIPA; DHCP console indicates unauthorized state or event logs show authorization failure.
workflow.diagnosis: DHCP server is not authorized in Active Directory.
workflow.fix: DHCP MMC → right-click server → Authorize. Restart DHCP service if needed and confirm authorized status.

tickets.title: Option inheritance applies wrong default gateway
tickets.summary: Clients in 10.90.2.0/24 receive gateway for 10.90.1.0/24 and cannot route.

workflow.triage: Clients have IP but cannot reach outside subnet; default gateway is wrong.
workflow.diagnosis: Option 003 (Router) is configured at the wrong level, overriding per-scope settings.
workflow.fix: DHCP MMC: remove conflicting server-level option and set option 003 correctly at each scope.

tickets.title: Relay configured but blocked by firewall/ACLs (UDP 67/68)
tickets.summary: IP helper is configured and scope exists, but clients still fail DHCP after new firewall rules.

workflow.triage: Some requests never arrive; clients remain on APIPA.
workflow.diagnosis: Firewall/ACL is blocking DHCP relay traffic between gateway and DHCP server (UDP 67/68).
workflow.fix: Allow DHCP relay traffic between relay and DHCP server; verify routing and symmetry.

validations: Firewall logs show no DHCP drops
